idiom_name: ReentrantReadWriteLock: readLock()/writeLock() with lock()/unlock() in try/finally
implementation_notes: java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantReadWriteLock implements ReadWriteLock: readLock()/writeLock() return Lock objects, both modes are reentrant, an optional fair constructor argument replaces the default throughput-oriented policy with arrival-order queueing, and a writer may take the read lock (downgrade) while a reader may not take the write lock (upgrade is impossible). Choose it for read-mostly collections and caches where readers would otherwise queue on a single Lock; choose StampedLock when read sections are short and optimistic validation is affordable.
pitfalls: A read lock can never be upgraded: acquiring the write lock while holding the read lock blocks forever; release the read lock (and re-validate) first.
Fair mode is much slower under high contention; use it only when starvation is proven, and remember that tryLock() ignores the fairness setting.
Read locks do not make the returned objects safe: a getter that hands out mutable internals lets a reader mutate state under a read lock.
Downgrading requires acquiring the read lock before releasing the write lock and is easy to get backwards.

variants.name: StampedLock with optimistic reads (Java 8+)
variants.idiom_name: StampedLock: tryOptimisticRead() + validate(), writeLock()/readLock() by stamp
variants.implementation_notes: StampedLock replaces guards with stamps: tryOptimisticRead() returns a stamp without blocking, validate(stamp) reports whether a writer intervened, and tryConvertToWriteLock(stamp) upgrades when possible; locks may be released or converted by another thread because there is no ownership. It is designed for short read paths inside thread-safe components rather than as a general Lock, and it is not reentrant.
pitfalls: Optimistic reads may observe inconsistent state: copy fields into locals and retry when validate() fails.
Not reentrant and not ownership based; a stamp must be released only in the mode that produced it, and a thread that never took a lock must not unlock.
Stamps are not cryptographically secure and can recycle after very long uptime; they are not a remote-locking mechanism.
